the-mad-podcast-with-matt-turck.name: The MAD Podcast with Matt Turck
the-mad-podcast-with-matt-turck.bio: Podcast: OpenAI's Dan Roberts: Why AI Can Now Make Discoveries

html_en:
AI is quietly crossing a threshold — from tool to autonomous collaborator — and today's dispatches from researchers, builders, and product teams show just how fast that transition is happening.

🧠 The Science Machine Awakens

The week's most intellectually arresting conversation comes from The MAD Podcast, where Matt Turck sits down with Dan Roberts, who leads the foundations of reinforcement learning team at OpenAI. The backdrop: OpenAI, DeepMind, and Anthropic have all recently cracked versions of the long-unsolved Erdős problems in mathematics — a moment Roberts calls genuinely thrilling.

"I feel really excited that we will get to really answer a lot of fundamental questions in the field of science that we care about with the aid — or the models being the driving force. And so that's just really thrilling."
— Dan Roberts, OpenAI

Roberts traces a fascinating intellectual arc: from a MIT PhD studying quantum gravity and black holes, through a postdoc at the Institute for Advanced Study, to writing The Principles of Deep Learning Theory, and ultimately joining OpenAI to work at the frontier. His core insight — that deep learning lives in the same statistical physics framework used to understand thermodynamics — explains why physicists keep ending up in AI labs.

What makes his team's work particularly notable is the mandate: not just to make reinforcement learning work, but to understand why it works, and to map its scaling laws.

"One of the advantages to being first… is that you can empower a group of people to not just work on making the thing work, but work on understanding how it works."
— Dan Roberts
Watch/Listen: OpenAI's Dan Roberts: Why AI Can Now Make Discoveries — The MAD Podcast

🤖 Agents That Dream, Self-Correct, and Remember

Anthropic quietly dropped one of its most ambitious product updates in months. The new Claude Managed Agents release introduces three capabilities that together sketch a picture of what genuinely autonomous AI workflows look like: dreaming, outcomes, and multiagent orchestration.

Dreaming is the headline. It's a scheduled background process that reviews past agent sessions, extracts patterns across them, and refines the agent's memory — so it gets better between runs, not just within them. Outcomes lets developers write a rubric for success; a separate grader evaluates results against it and sends the agent back for another pass if needed. In internal benchmarks, outcomes improved task success by up to 10 points, with notable gains on file generation (+8.4% on .docx, +10.1% on .pptx). And multiagent orchestration lets a lead agent delegate parallelized subtasks to specialists, each with their own model, prompt, and toolset.

The real-world deployments are striking. Harvey's legal agents saw completion rates jump roughly 6x with dreaming enabled. Netflix built an analysis agent that processes logs from hundreds of builds simultaneously. And Spiral by Every uses a Haiku lead agent to coordinate subagents running on Opus — with every draft scored against an editorial rubric before it's returned to the user.

This is the agentic stack becoming real infrastructure, not demo-ware.

⚙️ The Platform Wars: Vercel, Replit, and the Compute Convergence

On the infrastructure front, Guillermo Rauch has been having a big week. Vercel shipped longer function runtimes — what he calls "an innocent tweak of a constant" that is actually the payoff of a multi-year platform investment in microVM-based Fluid compute.

"A sandbox. A function. A server. A build. Are you getting it!? These are all expressions of the same underlying compute infrastructure. 2026 is the year serverless and servers finally converge. With no gotchas."
— @rauchg

Meanwhile, Amjad Masad is bullish on Replit's domain-specific agents — a growth agent surfacing SEO issues, a security agent flagging vulnerabilities — and particularly loves the "select all, fix with Agent" workflow. And Peter Yang made a provocative observation about OpenAI's Codex:

"Codex browser use is so good that it almost makes me forget APIs are even needed."
— @petergyang

📱 Gemini Gets a Better Ear

Josh Woodward from Google announced a quietly significant update to the Gemini app's voice input: the mic icon now supports 70+ languages, lets users mix languages freely mid-conversation, and requires no language setting changes. It's coming to web in about a week. For non-English speakers — a majority of the world — this is the kind of friction removal that actually changes behavior.

Google also opened limited slots for a Gemini Trusted Tester program, giving power users early access to unreleased features.

🏛️ The Regulation Debate Sharpens

Aaron Levie offered one of the cleaner articulations of why model-level AI regulation is likely to fail — and why use-case regulation is the more coherent path.

"The capabilities of AI models have near infinite permutations. It's going to be very hard to have a purely objective set of metrics that can be universally applied before every model release… Now, imagine this same process with every country that you're doing business with, globally, for every single model release. This is why we need to primarily focus on regulating the applied uses of AI, where the risk actually shows up."
— @levie

He also flagged a piece worth reading on the customization thesis:

"The companies that win won't necessarily be the ones with the biggest models. They'll be the ones that turn intelligence into something uniquely their own."
— via @levie

The open-source subplot continues to simmer. Swyx reminded the timeline that "goblingate" — whatever Mistral-adjacent drama that entailed — was already 1.5 months ago. In internet time, ancient history. Levie, for his part, is simply bullish on open source winning big. Meanwhile, Amjad Masad quipped: "Who needs Fable when you can have Mistral's Le Chaton Fat" — a reminder that model naming remains the industry's most underrated art form.
html_zh:
AI 系统正在从被动执行任务转向主动发现、自我改进与自主决策——从解开数学难题到"梦境"式的跨会话学习，这一周的进展令人目不转睛。

🧠 AI 的科学突破时刻：从解题工具到发现引擎

本周最值得深思的对话，来自 The MAD Podcast with Matt Turck，嘉宾是 OpenAI 强化学习基础团队负责人 Dan Roberts。他的背景颇为独特——MIT 理论物理博士，研究黑洞与量子引力，后来转向 AI，将统计物理的工具引入深度学习理论。

访谈的核心议题，是 OpenAI、DeepMind 与 Anthropic 近期联手攻克了数学界著名的 Erdős 难题——这被许多人视为 AI 从"完成人类交代的任务"跨越到"自主推进科学发现"的里程碑时刻。

"我非常期待，我们将能够真正回答科学领域许多基础性问题，而模型将成为这一过程的核心驱动力。这真的令人心潮澎湃。" —— Dan Roberts

Roberts 强调，强化学习之所以能实现这种"逆向思考"，在于模型可以假设某个命题为假，然后沿着漫长的推理链坚持下去——而这需要极强的内在确信。Watch/Listen: OpenAI's Dan Roberts: Why AI Can Now Make Discoveries

🤖 Claude 的"梦境"：自我进化的 Agent 架构

Anthropic 悄然推出了一项令人着迷的新能力。在其最新博客 New in Claude Managed Agents 中，"dreaming"（梦境）功能正式亮相——这是一个定期运行的后台进程，回顾历史会话、提炼规律、更新记忆，让 Agent 在两次任务之间持续自我改进。

"记忆让每个 Agent 在工作中记录所学；梦境则在会话间隙提炼这些记忆，汇聚多个 Agent 的共同经验，并保持其高度有效。"

此外，新推出的 outcomes（成果评估） 功能让开发者可以写下"成功标准"，由独立的评分器判断输出是否达标，未达标则让 Agent 重新尝试。内部测试显示，这一机制在最难的任务上将成功率提升了最多 10 个百分点。

实际应用案例同样亮眼：Harvey 的法律写作 Agent 完成率在测试中提升约 6 倍；Netflix 用多 Agent 并行分析数百次构建的日志；写作工具 Spiral 则用 Haiku 模型统筹调度、Opus 模型负责实际创作，并以 outcomes 对每篇草稿进行质量把关。

🛠️ 开发者工具军备竞赛：从 Vercel 到 Replit

基础设施层面同样热闹非凡。Guillermo Rauch 宣布 Vercel 函数运行时限制大幅延长，并将其定位为一次多年平台投资的收官之作：

"沙盒、函数、服务器、构建——你明白了吗？这些不过是同一底层计算基础设施的不同表现形式。2026 年，serverless 与 server 将真正融合，不再有任何隐患。" —— @rauchg

与此同时，Amjad Masad 对 Replit 的领域专属 Agent 赞不绝口——一个负责浮现 SEO 问题，另一个专注安全漏洞扫描，"全选、用 Agent 修复"的交互方式让他爱不释手。他还对 OpenAI Codex 的浏览器能力印象深刻：

"Codex 的浏览器使用体验好到让我几乎忘记 API 的存在。" —— @petergyang

📱 Gemini 的多语言麦克风与开放测试计划

Google Gemini 团队的 Josh Woodward 带来了一项对非英语用户极为友好的更新：Gemini App 的麦克风功能现已支持 70+ 种语言，无需切换语言设置，可自由混用多语言，且不会打断用户说话。

"我们的麦克风图标在 Android 和 iOS 上大幅升级！这对非英语用户来说是巨大突破。" —— @joshwoodward

此外，Gemini 正在开放有限名额的「Trusted Tester」计划，邀请重度用户抢先体验未公开功能。网页版支持预计将于一周内上线。

⚖️ AI 监管：别学 FDA，管应用而非模型

在政策讨论上，Box CEO Aaron Levie 给出了一针见血的判断。他认为"为 AI 设立 FDA"的思路在实践中将是灾难性的：

"AI 模型的能力组合有近乎无限的排列方式。很难在每次模型发布前，在模型实验室、学术界与政府之间，建立一套纯客观、可普遍适用的评估指标体系……再乘以全球每个国家，再乘以几十款模型的发布积压——你很快就能看到，这在极端情况下将戏剧性地拖慢整个 AI 进步。这就是为什么我们应该聚焦于监管 AI 的具体应用——风险真正显现的地方。" —— @levie

他同时转发了一篇关于智能定制化趋势的文章，并评论道："赢家未必是拥有最大模型的公司，而是那些能将智能转化为独特自身优势的公司。" 在开源与闭源的长期博弈中，他也明确站队：开源将大获全胜。
